region: Penn Yan · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Red Tail Ridge is the winery of Nancy Irelan and Mike Schnelle on the west shore of Seneca Lake, about ten miles south of Geneva. Irelan, the winemaker, came east from California, where she was vice president of viticulture and enology research at Gallo; Schnelle runs the business and vineyard. They planted Pinot Noir and Riesling first, then a run of cool-climate reds rarely seen in New York, including Teroldego, Lagrein and Blaufränkisch. Their winery was the first in New York to earn LEED Gold certification, heated and cooled by geothermal energy.

This Blaufränkisch, the dark-skinned grape of Austria and Central Europe, comes from the RTR estate vineyard, about 35 acres on Seneca Lake’s western slope, where lake breezes temper the climate over limestone-rich soils. Irelan’s cellar leans organic and natural: most fermentations use native yeasts, sulfur at bottling is kept low, and the reds are never filtered. Part of the wine ages in neutral oak, which adds a subtle smokiness without masking the fruit.

Expect a medium-bodied, cool-climate red with bright acidity and fine tannins rather than heft. Rose petal, black pepper and plum, with cranberry and blackberry on the palate, reflect the grape’s peppery, juicy character; it takes well to a slight chill. It is lovely with roast poultry, grilled mushrooms or lamb; fans of Cabernet Franc or northern Rhône Syrah will find familiar ground.
